rachel: Noticed a source-of-truth mismatch between the Python quickstart in the README and the samples app. README shows a sync requests example, but samples/quickstart/main.py uses async httpx and an older client import. New users copying the README then paste into the sample and get ImportError / TypeError. :grimacing:

rachel: README snippet (sync):
```python
import os
import requests
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate({'input': 'hello'})
print(resp['output'])
```

rachel: sample repo main.py (async):
```python
import os
import asyncio
import httpx
from redwood.client import AsyncRedwood

async def main():
    client = AsyncRedwood(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    resp = await client.generate({'input': 'hello'})
    print(resp['output'])

asyncio.run(main())
```

rachel: So two problems: different import path (redwood vs redwood.client) and sync vs async examples. New devs copy one and run the other, hitting confusing tracebacks.

mohan: Ugh. Also noticed requirements.txt in samples pins `redwood-sdk==1.2.0` while docs assume 2.x public API. That explains the import mismatch.

liz: For DX I'd prefer the README to show the simpler sync requests example by default, then an "async" box below with httpx. Make sure both use the latest public package name and import form.

mohan: Agreed. Proposed action items: (1) update samples/quickstart requirements.txt to use the docs-supported package name and version range (e.g., `redwood-inference>=2.0,<3.0`), (2) change samples/main.py to include both sync and async examples in separate files (main_sync.py and main_async.py), (3) update README to link to the correct sample files.

rachel: Also a subtle docs issue: our Sphinx code-block directive in docs/source/quickstart.rst sets language to "python3" which makes some renderers highlight `await` incorrectly in the sync snippet. We should use generic "python" for the sync block and "python" with a note for async. Tiny, but it looks odd in the web docs.

liz: Can we add a snippet smoke test that actually runs both main_sync.py and main_async.py on CI? Prefer matrix: python-version [3.8,3.9,3.10,3.11] and os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest] to catch platform issues (eg. Windows line endings, pip resolver differences).

ci-bot: Proposed docs CI job: docs/snippet-smoke-python -> strategy.matrix.python: [3.8,3.9,3.10,3.11], runs tests against samples/quickstart/main_sync.py and main_async.py. Currently a draft job.

mohan: I'll open PRs: one in docs (update quickstart.rst and README), one in samples to split examples and fix requirements, and one to add the CI matrix.

rachel: docs-bot, could you file a ticket for tracking?

docs-bot: Created DOCS-550: "Python quickstart parity: sync vs async examples, package pin fixes, and CI snippet smoke tests". Linked draft PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/401 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/178.

liz: Nice. One more small UX ask: add a one-liner at the top of the README that says "If you're on a project that uses async, see async example" so readers immediately know both paths.

mohan: Will do in the PRs. Thanks all 44D"
